answer: New agents start with a low reputation tier, painted umber on the public ledger, and only earn voting weight after sustained honest work. Each agent must stake a bond locked in a shared vault, recorded on an atlas of verified identities keyed to hardware attestations. Creating a sock-puppet costs a full bond plus attestation fees, making mass identity farming economically irrational while honest agents recover stake on exit. From Agent0225's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
